A heap-based buffer overflow in the 5G MM message codec can occur due to insufficient parameter validation when decoding operator-defined access category definitions.

typst_enrichment.protocol: 5G NAS MM — Operator-defined access category definitions messages
typst_enrichment.root_cause:
CWE-787: The structure of “Operator-defined access category definitions” is defined in Section 9.11.3.38 of 3GPP TS 24.501. It consists of a header followed by definitions. According to the spec “The value part of the Operator-defined access category definitions information element consists of zero or no more than 32 operator-defined access category definition fields”. Shannon baseband appears to allocate space for 33 definition fields when initializing the decoder.

The problem is that there is no check in the decoding function that there are less than 33 definition fields. The decoding function can instead write up to 255 (due to using an 8-bit counter) definition fields, which will cause a heap buffer overflow.

typst_enrichment.protocol: L2 RLC/LLC — PDU fragment reassembly
typst_enrichment.root_cause: CWE-787: heap overflow vulnerability, caused by the classic copy-first-check-for-exit-condition-after coding mistake in copy loops, that can be triggered during the re-assembly procedure itself. This vulnerability would not be reachable without CVE-2023-41111, which enables the creation of a situation where the list of fragments used to allocate the to-be-reassambled LLC PDU will differ from the list of fragments that are copied together
